thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: elevated 5xx rate detected for service=infra-inference-gateway (us-west-2) 
incident-bot: symptom: 5xx surge starting ~2026-03-15T11:02:10Z, p50 latency unaffected, error spike to ~5.4% of requests, errors=502/504/503. Paging oncall.
oncall-alice: I'm paged, grabbing context. Which customers impacted?
helen-support: Seeing multiple alerts from customer dashboards — a few high-QPS customers (acme-enterprises, dataflow.ai) reporting timeouts. Support ticket #INC-5829 opened.
carol-sre: Oncall, check envoy stats on gateways: curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:19000/stats?filter=cluster.*" | grep -E "5xx|upstream_rq|cx_overflow"
carol-sre: I'm seeing big upstream 5xx counts and upstream_rq_pending_overflow for cluster "svc-inference-backend-v2"
dmitry-eng: FYI: there was a loadbalancer/route rollout at 11:01 by deploy-bot (change_id=chg-20260315-1101) — it adjusted route weights and retry_policy for gateway routes.
dmitry-eng: suspecting new route weight + retry policy causing retry amplification -> circuitbreaker tripping downstream.
oncall-alice: Can we get the exact new route fragment? deploy-bot, show the change diff.
deploy-bot: change_id=chg-20260315-1101 deployed by dmitry-eng. Diff snippet: 
```
- route {
-  name: "inference-v2"
-  weighted_clusters: { clusters: { name: "svc-inference-backend-v2", weight: 80 }, { name: "svc-inference-backend-v1", weight: 20 } }
-  retry_policy: { retry_on: "5xx,connect-failure,refused-stream", num_retries: 1 }
-  per_filter_config: {
-    envoy.filters.http.circuit_breaker: { max_connections: 100, max_pending_requests: 50 }
-  }
+ route {
+  name: "inference-v2"
+  weighted_clusters: { clusters: { name: "svc-inference-backend-v2", weight: 95 }, { name: "svc-inference-backend-v1", weight: 5 } }
+  retry_policy: { retry_on: "5xx,connect-failure,refused-stream", num_retries: 2 }
+  per_filter_config: {
+    envoy.filters.http.circuit_breaker: { max_connections: 60, max_pending_requests: 10 }
+  }
 }
```
carol-sre: Ok that matches: increased weight to v2 and bumped retries from 1->2 while tightening circuit-breaker. That can definitely amplify 5xx if v2 is returning intermittent 502s. Retries + lower CB thresholds -> cascade.
helen-support: Customer impact estimate from telemetry: ~12 customers saw >10% error rate spike, top 5 customers consumed ~42% of affected requests. We're getting inbound escalations from acme-enterprises.
oncall-alice: Mitigation plan — immediate steps: 1) Disable retries on gateway route, 2) revert route weight back to previous (80/20), 3) temporarily relax circuit-breaker to avoid drops while we debug backend v2.
carol-sre: Agreed. I'll push a quick config patch to set retry_policy.num_retries=0 for that route and bump pending_requests to 200. Doing via config-service: 
```
curl -X POST "https://configsvc.internal/v1/routes/replace" -d '{"change_id":"mit-848","route":"inference-v2","retry_policy":{"num_retries":0},"circuit_breaker":{"max_pending_requests":200}}'
```
carol-sre: applying now...
carol-sre: apply succeeded, rolling config across 4 edge proxies in us-west-2 (rolling update).
carol-sre: Confirming envoy stats after patch... upstream_rq_pending_overflow for svc-inference-backend-v2 dropping to 0, upstream_rq_5xx_rate decreasing.
dmitry-eng: I'll roll back the weight change to 80/20 with rollout API to be safe: 
```
curl -X POST "https://deploy.internal/rollout/rollback" -d '{"change_id":"chg-20260315-1101"}'
```
dmitry-eng: rollback triggered, deploy-bot: starting traffic-rebalance to previous weights.
deploy-bot: rollback requested, rolling out config to LB fleet (us-west-2). Estimated convergence ~30s.
oncall-alice: Support, prepare customer comms for acme-enterprises and dataflow.ai — state we're incident responding and have mitigation; give ETA ~30min for full stabilization.
helen-support: Drafting messages now. Will post to their support threads.
carol-sre: Monitoring metrics: error rate down from 5.4% -> 1.1% within 90s of disabling retries and weight rollback. P50 latency stable. No additional 5xx spikes.
oncall-alice: Good. Are there any pods in backend v2 showing OOM or restart loops? kubectl -n backend get pods -l app=inference-v2 -o wide
dmitry-eng: No restarts, logs show a small surge of 502s from backend service due to a dependency (redis connection saturation) — we think v2 is more sensitive to transient upstream load.
carol-sre: For immediate: keep retries disabled on gateway for 30m, maintain weight rollback until backend patch/mitigation done. We'll also increase CB thresholds on the gateway permanently until backend fix is validated.
oncall-alice: I'm going to remain on this incident. Handing to SRE/infra for root cause and postmortem. If anyone else needs to take over, say now.
dmitry-eng: I'll own the backend fix + load testing to validate v2. Plan: revert resource limits on v2 replica set and add connection pooling improvements.
helen-support: Logged customer impact summary: 5.4% global 5xx at peak, ~120k failed requests during the window, ~12 customers with >10% errors; top affected: acme-enterprises (20% of their requests failed), dataflow.ai (13%).
oncall-alice: OK — incident status: mitigated (live mitigation applied) — continuing monitoring. Next steps: postmortem, permanent rollback or adjusted route config, backend v2 hardening, and update playbook to avoid retries + tight CB combos.
incident-bot: Incident ticket INC-5829 updated: status=mitigated, severity=sev2, assignees=[oncall-alice,dmitry-eng,carol-sre], sla-impact: partial (customer-facing errors).
carol-sre: adding notes to playbook: when deploying route weight changes, avoid increasing retries simultaneously and ensure canary health checks include upstream dependency saturation signals.
oncall-alice: Thanks team. Handoff to SRE for postmortem. I'll remain available for 15m then hand to carol-sre.
carol-sre: Acknowledged, taking primary for postmortem and RCA writeup.
helen-support: I'll follow up in customer tickets with mitigation summary and ETA for a permanent fix.
incident-bot: thread closed for paging; monitoring will re-open if error rate rises above 2% again."
